values.description: The base URL for the API. Set to 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1' for Local development, 'https://staging.example.com/api/v1' for Staging, and 'https://api.example.com/api/v1' for Production.
API Key for authentication. Replace with environment-specific keys (e.g., 'YOUR_STAGING_API_KEY', 'YOUR_PRODUCTION_API_KEY'). This key grants access to the API.
Default username for authentication in the current environment. Adjust for Staging/Production environments to use appropriate test or production user credentials.
Default password for authentication in the current environment. Adjust for Staging/Production environments. **Never commit actual production passwords.**

Bearer token obtained after successful login (e.g., via OAuth2 or JWT). This variable should be set dynamically by a login request. It will differ across environments and user sessions and typically has a short expiry.
Refresh token obtained after successful login, used to get new access tokens when the current one expires. Set dynamically by a login request. Longer lived than access tokens.
OAuth2 Client ID. Use environment-specific values (e.g., 'staging_oauth_client_id', 'prod_oauth_client_id') for different application registrations.
OAuth2 Client Secret. Use environment-specific values (e.g., 'staging_oauth_client_secret', 'prod_oauth_client_secret'). **Keep this secret and do not expose it publicly.**
OAuth2 scopes required for the application. These define the permissions granted to the client. May vary slightly by environment or client configuration.
Email for an administrative user in the current environment. Useful for testing admin-specific endpoints. Adjust for Staging/Production.
Password for an administrative user in the current environment. Adjust for Staging/Production. **Handle with care.**
A sample user ID for testing specific endpoints that require a user context. Adjust as needed for different environments or test cases.
A sample product ID for testing specific product-related endpoints. Adjust as needed for different environments or test cases.
A sample order ID for testing specific order-related endpoints. Adjust as needed for different environments or test cases.
